content.title: March Madness: Each college basketball coach's salary in Sweet 16
content.text: Arkansas' John Calipari (left), Houston's Kelvin Sampson (center) and UConn's Dan Hurley (right) are some of the highest-paid college basketball coaches with teams playing in the 2026 NCAA Tournament's Sweet 16.Getty ImagesThis is no Sweet 16 for Cinderellas, and it certainly doesn’t feature a field of coaches who are severely underpaid.Of the 16 remaining teams in March Madness, only two are worse than a six seed — No. 9 Iowa and No. 11 Texas — and both of those schools have well-funded athletic departments.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢So, when you’re watching the region semifinal games, which tip off Thursday, you’ll see some of the most well-compensated coaches in the sport. Eleven of the 16 coaches still in the tournament make at least $5 million per year, led by UConn’s Dan Hurley, who signed a six-year, $50 million contract when the Lakers tried to woo him away from the college game after he won his second of back-to-back national titles in 2024.Article continues below this adKeep in mind, those salaries are only going to increase this offseason, especially with high-profile openings at North Carolina and possibly Kansas sure to help secure raises for several big-name coaches.Only two of the coaches with teams still playing — Arkansas' John Calipari and Tennessee’s Rick Barnes — have more career wins than University of Houston’s Kelvin Sampson, so it makes sense that Sampson is right up there among the highest-paid coaches, checking in at No. 5 among the Sweet 16 teams.Houston Chronicle LogoMake us a Preferred Source on Google to see more of us when you search.Add Preferred SourceHere are the annual salaries for each coach in this year’s NCAA Tournament Sweet 16… Dan Hurley, UConn: $8.3 millionUConn head coach Dan Hurley calls out to his team during the second half in the first round of the NCAA college basketball tournament against Furman, Saturday, March 21, 2026, in Philadelphia. (AP Photo/Matt Rourke)Matt Rourke/Associated PressNote: Hurley signed a six-year, $50 million deal in 2024 that averages out to $8.3 million per yearSource: New York TimesArticle continues below this adJohn Calipari, Arkansas: $7.5 millionArkansas head coach John Calipari calls for a coach's challenge during the second half in the second round of the NCAA college basketball tournament against High Point, Saturday, March 21, 2026, in Portland, Ore. (AP Photo/Amanda Loman)Amanda Loman/Associated PressNote: Calipari’s base salary is $7 million with an annual $500,000 retention paymentSource: USA TodayTom Izzo, Michigan State: $7.2 millionMichigan State head coach Tom Izzo celebrates during the second half against Louisville in the second round of the NCAA college basketball tournament, Saturday, March 21, 2026, in Buffalo, N.Y. (AP Photo/Jeffrey T. Barnes)Jeffrey T. Barnes/Associated PressArticle continues below this adJon Scheyer, Duke: $7 millionDuke head coach Jon Scheyer yells to his players during the first half in the second round of the NCAA college basketball tournament against TCU, Saturday, March 21, 2026, in Greenville, S.C. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson)Brynn Anderson/Associated PressNote: Scheyer signed a new contract in October that is estimated at $7 million per year, but Duke is a private school and not subject to open records requests.Source: Yahoo SportsRick Barnes, Tennessee: $6 millionTennessee head coach Rick Barnes reacts to play against Vanderbilt during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game in the quarterfinal round of the Southeastern Conference tournament, Friday, March 13, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (AP Photo/George Walker IV)George Walker IV/Associated PressArticle continues below this adKelvin Sampson, Houston: $5.5 millionHouston head coach Kelvin Sampson instructs players during the first half in the second round of the NCAA college basketball tournament in Oklahoma City, Saturday, March 21, 2026.Brett Coomer/Houston ChronicleNate Oats, Alabama: $5.5 millionAlabama head coach Nate Oats calls a play against Hofstra during the second half in the first round of the NCAA college basketball tournament Friday, March 20, 2026, in Tampa, Fla. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)Chris O'Meara/Associated PressArticle continues below this adBrad Underwood, Illinois: $5.5 millionIllinois head coach Brad Underwood watches during the second half against VCU in the second round of the NCAA college basketball tournament, Saturday, March 21, 2026, in Greenville, S.C. (AP Photo/Chris Carlson)Chris Carlson/Associated PressNote: Underwood’s base salary is $4.4 million, but gets a $1.1 million performance-based retention bonus this summerSource: ESPNSean Miller, Texas: $5.3 millionTexas head coach Sean Miller reacts on the sideline during the first half in the first round of the NCAA college basketball tournament against BYU, Thursday, March 19, 2026, in Portland, Ore. (AP Photo/Travis Heying)Travis Heying/Associated PressRick Pitino, St John’s: $3.3 millionSt. John's head coach Rick Pitino reacts during the second half of a game against Kansas in the second round of the NCAA college basketball tournament Sunday, March 22, 2026, in San Diego. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill)Mark J. Terrill/Associated PressNote: St. John’s has offered Pitino a raise and a new three-year contract that he said he will look at after the season.Source: NJ.com
